notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: Some people followed what the devils recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman.
Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery.
They also followed what was sent down upon the pair of angels in Babil, Harut and Marut.
They did not teach anyone until they had said that they were only a trial, and that he should therefore not disbelieve.
People learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, and they harm no one by it except by God's permission.
They learned what harms them and does not benefit them, and they knew that whoever buys it has no share in the Hereafter, and wretched is what they sold themselves for, if only they knew.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah says that some people followed what the devils recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman, and that Sulayman did not disbelieve [c1][c2]. It also says that they followed what was sent down upon the pair of angels in Babil, Harut and Marut, who taught no one until they had said that they were only a trial [c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: Some people followed what the devils recited concerning the kingdom of Sulayman [c1]. Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery [c2]. They also followed what was sent down upon the pair of angels in Babil, Harut and Marut [c3]. They did not teach anyone until they had said that they were only a trial, and that he should therefore not disbelieve [c4]. People learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife, and they harm no one by it except by God's permission [c5]. They learned what harms them and does not benefit them, and they knew that whoever buys it has no share in the Hereafter, and wretched is what they sold themselves for, if only they knew [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah is one long sentence, and it does not say who the people are who followed what the devils recited [c1]. The Arabic word for the pair can be read as angels or as kings in different recitations [c3]. The Arabic word ma can be read as what or as not, and the sense of the clause changes with it [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Sulayman did not disbelieve [c2]. The ayah says that Harut and Marut told anyone who came to them that they were only a trial, so that he should not disbelieve [c4]. It says that whoever buys what harms him has no share in the Hereafter [c6].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah separates Sulayman from disbelief and puts the teaching of sorcery on the devils [c2]. Another is that it presents what people learned as harming them and not benefiting them [c6].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the people are who followed what the devils recited, or when this happened.
- Not established: whether the Arabic is to be read as angels or kings, or whether what was sent down is affirmed or denied; the recitations and the readers differ, and this draft does not choose.
- Not established: where Babil was, or what the trial consisted of.
- Not established: anything about their nature, what they taught beyond the words of the ayah, or what became of them.

uncertainties_en: Many accounts about Harut and Marut circulate in later works; none is used here, and this draft adds nothing to what the one ayah states.
Hadith to add later: reports about Harut and Marut are numerous and graded differently; each would need a named grader, with the text of the ayah as the control; none is used here.
